courses.subject: SLAV
courses.title: Introduction to Slavic Languages and Peoples
courses.description: This undergraduate course introduces students to the languages and culture of the western, southern, and eastern Slavic worlds. The course leverages language and culture to approach the relationship between nation and state. No prior knowledge of a Slavic language is needed.

courses.subject: SLAV
courses.title: Childhood and Adolescence in Slavic Literature
courses.description: Childhood and adolescence as portrayed in both fictional and autobiographical form by 19th-and 20th-century Russian, Polish, Czech, and other East European writers, including Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Nabokov, I. B. Singer, Schulz, Milosz. Lectures and readings in English. Honors version available.

courses.subject: SLAV
courses.title: Introduction to Non-Russian Slavic/East European Culture
courses.description: Reading and discussion of selected authors in the target language aimed at improving reading and analytical skills and preparing the student for higher level work.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, BULG 404, CZCH 404, HUNG 404, MACD 404, PLSH 404, or BCS 404; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: SLAV
courses.title: Songs of Liberty, Light, and Resilience: Ukrainian Literature Today
courses.description: Ukraine's resistance to Russian aggression brought renewed attention to Europe's largest country, its history, and its quest for liberty and democracy. This course explores the ways in which Ukrainian national identity has been forged by revolutions, wars, engineered famines as well as thirst for liberty. Works of Ukraine's leading writers will help students form an independent critical opinion of the country's unique culture, its problems, and aspirations. All materials are in English.

courses.subject: SLAV
courses.title: Directed Readings in a Slavic Language
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Directed readings in a Slavic language other than Russian on topics in literature and linguistics not normally covered in scheduled courses.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: SLAV
courses.title: Imagined Jews: Jewish Themes in Polish and Russian Literature
courses.description: Explores the fictional representation of Jewish life in Russia and Poland by Russian, Polish, and Jewish authors from the 19th century to the present. Taught in English; some foreign language readings for qualified students.

courses.subject: SLAV
courses.title: Coming to America: New York in Yiddish Literature and Culture
courses.description: New York was a significant gateway for immigration to the United States, particularly for Jews from Eastern Europe in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. As a result, the city became the world's capital of Yiddish culture. This course explores the vibrant world of Yiddish literature, theater, poetry, journalism, and political activism that flourished in New York, shaping its unique ''Nyu-Yorkrish'' qualities. Through a diverse selection of texts, we will trace the evolution of Yiddish creativity in America's cultural capital. Readings and class discussions in English.

source.text: SLAV 469. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | JWST 469 .

courses.subject: SLAV
courses.title: 20th-Century Russian and Polish Theater
courses.description: A comparative survey of the major trends in 20th-century Russian and Polish dramaturgy and theatrical production, with attention to aesthetic, professional, and political connections between the two. Taught in English; some foreign language readings for qualified students.

courses.subject: SLAV
courses.title: Topics in Slavic Culture
courses.description: Comparative study of topics in non-Russian Slavic literatures and culture not covered in any other course. Specific topics will vary and will be announced in advance. Taught in English; some foreign language readings for qualified students.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.
